title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page numbered 33 with a few handwritten corrections. It is not Grothendieck's handwriting, and it has nothing to do with the neighbouring handwritten pages on motivic Galois groups and crystalline/Hodge fibre functors. It is a page from a typescript on the cohomological purity theorem and fundamental (cycle) classes in étale cohomology for smooth pairs. The numbering and content match the 'théorème de pureté cohomologique relative' in SGA 4 Exposé XVI (M. Artin), §3, though this attribution is my inference.

Setting: S a base scheme and n invertible on S. Z ⊂ Y ⊂ X are closed immersions of S-smooth schemes, with v: Z→Y of codimension b, u: Y→X of codimension a, and w = u∘v of codimension c = a+b. The purity statement is twofold:
- R^q u^! vanishes for q ≠ 2a.
- There is a canonical isomorphism φ(Y,X): Z/n ≅ R^{2a}u^! μ_n^{⊗a}, the fundamental class of Y in X.

Because of the vanishing, the Grothendieck spectral sequence (R^p v^!)(R^q u^!)F ⇒ (R^{p+q}w^!)F degenerates and gives ξ: (R^{2b}v^!)(R^{2a}u^!)μ_n^{⊗c} ≅ (R^{2c}w^!)μ_n^{⊗c}. Transitivity (3.10.1) says that φ(Z,X) equals ξ ∘ η ∘ φ(Z,Y), where η = R^{2b}v^! applied to φ(Y,X)⊗μ_n^{⊗b}. In other words, the fundamental class of Z in X is the class of Z in Y followed by the Gysin/Thom class of Y in X.

The proof begins by induction on the codimension; c = 0 is trivial. For c = 1 the class is ε_t from (3.9), the Kummer-theory class attached to a local equation t of the divisor. One must show that ε_t is bijective and independent of t. This is étale-local on X and compatible with base change, as are the R^q i^! of (3.8). One can therefore check it fibre by fibre and reduce to S = Spec k with k separably closed. The argument continues on the next typescript page, which is not in this file.
errors: No mathematical errors. There are only French typing errors typical of a non-native author: 'se faite', 'commensons', 'le transitivité', 'indépendent', 'évident' for 'évidente', 'cet diagramme'.
The composition convention is implicit: the spectral sequence (R^p v^!)(R^q u^!) ⇒ R^{p+q} w^! requires w = u∘v, so w^! = v^! u^!. This is consistent with the diagram.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page from a typescript of standard published SGA 4-era material (relative purity and transitivity of fundamental classes), filed among unrelated handwritten notes. Its only interest is archival: a draft of SGA material surviving in the Grothendieck papers.
transcription_corrections: The typescript reads 'se faite' (typo in the original); 'se fait' is intended.
The typescript has 'commensons' (with an overstrike), intended 'commençons'.
'(3.8)' after '(R^q i^!)' is a handwritten insertion.
The diagram label '(3.10.1)' has an overstruck first character in the typescript.
'pout' is corrected to 'pour', and 'cela' is a handwritten correction of 'celq'.
'Z/n' appears as blackboard ℤ/n in the image; μ_n is typed as 'u_n' with a slash, i.e. ⁄μ_n.
The archive page number '65' is handwritten in the lower left corner.
